title: Skill evaluation scenario manifest (G37 Phase 0)
description: agent-evals/skills/scenarios.yaml. Category A scenarios reference an examples/ case and derive their expected outcome from examples/ground_truth.json; Category B scenarios carry invocation parameters that catalog cannot express.

id.description: Stable identifier. Appears in evidence bundle paths and in the expected-evidence set.

category.description: A = expected outcome resolvable from examples/ground_truth.json. B = needs invocation parameters that catalog cannot express.

status.description: ready = fixture resolves and the scenario contributes to the expected-evidence set. planned = declared but not yet runnable; excluded from expectations, and may not claim a resolvable fixture.

prompt.description: The verbatim request the agent sees. Never names abicheck (ADR-058 design principle 1).

case.description: Category A only: the examples/ case directory. Expected outcome is read from ground_truth.json, never restated here.

coverage_note.description: Which named D5 category this scenario covers, for the corpus-coverage test.

fixture.description: Category B only: repo-relative fixture directory.

platforms.description: Category B only: hosts this fixture actually supports, matching a Category A case's own PLATFORMS declaration. Omitted means unrestricted -- state it explicitly whenever the fixture's mechanics (a raw ELF .so build, a Linux-only toolchain assumption) are not actually portable, or a non-Linux runner executes it and the skill's own out-of-validated-scope NOT_VERIFIED response is graded against a concrete verdict it was never meant to produce.

architectures.description: Category B only: CPU architectures this fixture actually supports -- the identical restriction one axis over from `platforms`. Omitted means unrestricted, which is correct for a fixture that builds both sides from source on whichever host runs it (automatically architecture-consistent). State it explicitly only when the fixture ships a prebuilt, architecture-specific artifact (e.g. a committed .so) that a from-source side built on a different architecture would not actually match -- an OS-only `platforms` restriction (e.g. `[linux]`) does not by itself guarantee one architecture, since this repository's own CI runs both x86_64 and aarch64 Linux lanes.

invocation.description: Category B only: the parameters the catalog cannot express.

expected.description: Category B only: the outcome, stated here because no catalog owns it.

verdict.description: compare's ordinal verdict, or null for a pair that cannot be compared. For a consumer-scoped scenario (--used-by / --required-symbol) this is the *scoped* answer, matching where the CLI promotes it and what the skill instructs the agent to report — never the library-wide result.

full_verdict.description: Consumer-scoped scenarios only: the library-wide result the report preserves in `full_verdict`. Recorded because the interesting scenarios are exactly the ones where it diverges from `verdict`, and a grader that cannot see the distractor value cannot tell a correct scoped answer from an agent reading the report the wrong way round.

uncertainty.description: The D4 dimension-2 uncertainty kind this scenario exercises, if any. A scenario carrying one is what makes that zero-tolerance rule gated rather than notional.

then.comment: Category B-only fields. A Category A scenario restating a catalog-owned outcome is exactly the second copy the catalog exists to prevent -- platforms/architectures included, since those facts are already owned by the case's own PLATFORMS declaration in examples/ground_truth.json.
